## What it is about

*The article is written in Spanish, with an English abstract.*

The article maps the academic conversation at the intersection of corporate networks and the energy transition between 2015 and 2026. Using a cleaned Scopus corpus, it combines bibliometric co-occurrence analysis (titles and keywords), descriptive indicators and temporal trends, plus a terminology-sensitivity check.

The field is organised around a techno-climatic, implementation-oriented core: renewables, decarbonisation, energy policy and investment. Critical political-economy notions such as incumbency, lobbying, interlocking directorates and regulatory capture appear unevenly and, when present, sit on the periphery. The transition is framed mainly as a technological and management problem, while power and institutional influence are less integrated. The article proposes an agenda that combines bibliometrics with co-citation, collaboration networks and elite data (interlocks, ownership, politically exposed persons) to link power structures with decarbonisation pathways.
